# Researching and ingesting wiki evidence

Choose the mode explicitly from the request. An unspecified request to use this
role is not permission to process the whole backlog; clarify the intended task.
Treat `` as the request when the host has not substituted it.

- **Discover sources on a topic:** read [discovery](references/discover.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), and
  [efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md). Research perspectives
  return candidates without writing. Use the capture route only within the
  requested scope; a request for candidates alone remains read-only.
- **Capture named URLs or saved web pages:** read [named capture](references/capture.md)
  and [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Skip broad topic research;
  preserve deduplication, declines and capture checks.
- **Capture a named format or service:** read its complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or
  [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md). These routes include prerequisite
  checks; missing converters or authentication never justify fabricated evidence.
- **Ingest named existing clippings:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), and
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md). Use the exact source set;
  do not rediscover it or silently expand to the global backlog.
- **Process new or un-ingested clippings without a filename:** read
  [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join backlog contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Determine eligibility before writing. Preserve already summarized sources and
  reject restricted evidence as support. If nothing eligible is pending, report
  that without opening an operation, logging, committing or refreshing indexes.

Capture-only requests create evidence, never derived source or concept pages.
Ingestion needs authorization for that source set; an explicitly requested full
research-and-ingest flow already provides it. Only capture tools write raw
artifacts, and agents never edit their bodies. Read
[evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before assessing fidelity,
quoting or synthesizing; preserve restrictions and platform-specific sections.

Before the first authorized mutation, read
[operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md). Finish the
scoped validation, log, commit, sync and remote verification unless publication
is held. Reuse an enclosing operation when it owns the work; preserve other
writers' edits. For concept reuse and relationship changes read
[efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).

# Discover sources on a topic

Given a topic, find and independently assess sources that fill an evidence gap.
Perspective passes return candidates and never write the vault. A candidates-only
request stays read-only: report the selection without declines or captures. When
capture is within scope, use [capture and completion](capture.md#capture-the-selected-sources).
Ingestion is a separate authorized mode.

## Phase 0 — dedup before searching
Gather what the wiki already has so the search hunts for *gaps*, not dupes:
- Known source URLs: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs"` prints
  them, one per line, normalized as the clipper normalizes them (`--count` prints
  the number). It reads the clippings themselves (the first `source:` line of each
  file directly under `raw/clippings`), rather than querying an index built from
  them — the shortest path to the fact, and it stays correct while the index is
  stale. To ask about particular candidates, use
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs" --check "<url>" "<url>"`: one line
  per URL, in the order given, `new`, `clipped raw/clippings/<name>.md` (with
  ` (+N recapture)` when later captures of the page exist) or `declined: <reason>`.
  `--summary --topic "<topic>"` prints what a topic already holds. All three only read.
- Coverage summary: name the unanswered question, run bounded wiki searches, and
  read the relevant task MOC and leading concept/synthesis pages. Read only the
  manual Start here section of `index.md` if orientation is needed; do not load
  the generated catalog. List the known coverage and the specific evidence gap.
- Sanity-check the set: if the vault has clippings on disk but the known-URL
  set is empty, STOP — the collection step failed; do not proceed to search.
Pass the known-URL set + a one-line "already covered" summary to every perspective.

## Phase 1 — five perspective researchers (parallel if supported, else sequential)
Each perspective gets: the topic, the known-URL set, the coverage summary, and its
lens. Run them **in parallel if your host supports agent fan-out** — Claude Code:
dispatch five read-only agents in one message via the Agent tool; Copilot CLI: use
custom agents — **otherwise run the five lenses sequentially yourself.** Each runs
2–3 *varied* web searches, pre-skips any result whose domain is on the blocklist,
fetches the promising hits, and **returns a ranked candidate list** — it writes
nothing. Lenses:
- **Academic** — papers, textbooks, primary research, .edu.
- **Technical** — official docs, specs, standards, source repos.
- **Applied** — case studies, real-world usage, tutorials from practitioners.
- **News/Trends** — recent developments, reputable reporting (last ~2 years).
- **Contrarian** — critiques, failure modes, dissenting analysis.

Each candidate: `{ title, url, quality_guess: high|medium|low, key_findings,
why_ingest, adds_evidence, changes_page }`. `adds_evidence` names the unanswered
question it helps settle; `changes_page` names an existing or proposed concept
or synthesis. More material on an already answered question is not automatically
an improvement. Inspect existing high-use stubs and missing bridges before
requesting another broad collection run.

## Phase 2 — independent select + credibility (do NOT let a finder grade itself)
As the orchestrator (or a separate reviewer), over the pooled candidates:
1. Dedup by URL (normalize: drop `#fragment`, trailing `/`); drop any already in the
   known-URL set; drop blocked domains; drop any in the decline log
   (`.wiki-master/declined.json` — clip.mjs enforces this too, but skipping here
   saves re-arguing settled candidates).
2. Score each survivor with the rubric → `high | medium | low`:
   - +2 peer-reviewed / primary / official
   - +1 recent (≤3 yr) where recency matters
   - +1 known/credentialed author or authoritative org
   - +1 corroborated by another perspective's find (max +1)
   - −1 vendor-primary / promotional / single-blogger opinion
   Tiers: **high** ≥4, **medium** 2–3, **low** 0–1, **reject** <0 (don't clip).
3. Keep the top sources (favor `high`/`medium`; a few `low` are fine if on-topic).
   Reddit posts/comments and Medium articles are eligible; assess each source
   using the rubric, without treating votes as credibility. In the ranked report,
   group them under `## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and `## Medium articles`
   respectively, and carry those sections into ingestion per the
   [Reddit and Medium evidence policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md#reddit-and-medium).
4. **Only when capture is authorized, before the first decline or clip write**, open a discover operation with
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op discover` and retain its
   token using the host-specific completion example. Reuse that operation below, and
   pass its token as `--since <token>` on every clip: each clipper then records the exact
   path of every file it writes in the operation's ledger.
   **Record every reject** so it is never re-litigated:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --decline="<one-line reason>"`.
   "Seen, considered, declined" must have a representation — an unrecorded reject
   is indistinguishable from "never seen" and comes back every run. Declines
   expire after 180 days (TTL), so a changed world gets one re-evaluation.
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/decline.mjs" list` (`--json` for a machine reading)
   and `show "<url>"` read the log without changing it. `supersede "<url>" --reason "<why>"`
   ends an active decline without clipping anything; it is the only way to do so for a URL
   already in the vault, because `--supersede-decline` on a clip takes effect only when a
   clipping is written.

for approved-scope survivors, or return the candidate report for a research-only
request. Named URLs and saved files use [named capture](capture.md) directly.
# Vault access and host commands

Resolve the plugin root from the installed `SKILL.md` location, not the current
working directory: its containing skill folder's `../../` is the plugin root.
From a file in a skill's `references/` folder, use `../../../` instead.
Resolve and quote absolute helper paths before running commands. Treat
`$ARGUMENTS` as the user's request when the host has not substituted it. A linked
skill or reference can be read directly when the host has no skill loader; shared
policy does not require loading the maintenance-role entry point.
Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; with `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` set and no vault named, a script stops with exit 2 instead of using the default) and verify the expected
vault layout. Read local `AGENTS.md` and schema before edits. A known root and
filesystem access are sufficient for the supported operations below; do not ask
the user to restart Obsidian as a prerequisite for all work.

## Layout and read scope

`raw/clippings/` holds captured evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`
holds maintained pages; `moc/` holds navigational maps; `log/` holds one file per
operation. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it. Reads do not
open operations, write logs, commit or refresh indexes. Before any authorized
mutation, read [operation completion](operations.md); before quoting or
synthesizing, read [evidence](evidence.md).

Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs to the generated catalog. Search
diagnostics describe coverage, not relevance: a stale index can omit useful pages.
Read current passages and disclose weak or failed channels. Index freshness is
distinct from factual review dates.

## Choose the supported channel

| Operation | Channel and fallback |
|---|---|
| Read a Markdown page or source | CLI `read path=...`, or read its exact path under the known vault root. |
| Search | Prefer `search.mjs` and inspect its diagnostics. If a channel fails, use available results plus bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup. State missing channels. |
| Health, evidence routes, identity, relationships, drift coverage | Bundled filesystem helpers work without Obsidian. Do not gate them on `assertRunning`. Drift embeddings still require their backend. |
| Factual freshness report | `stale.mjs` may use CLI discovery or scoped filesystem fallback. Preserve missing-review and coverage diagnostics. |
| Ordinary Markdown creation/editing | Use exact-path filesystem edits even when the CLI is healthy, with the same operation, evidence, schema and validation contract. Read current content before editing; preserve unrelated changes. Never pass a whole note body through `content=`. |
| Small typed property or app actions | Use the guarded CLI entry point below; filesystem property edits remain available with schema validation. |
| Opening a note in the UI, executing an Obsidian/plugin command, app state, live Bases queries | Requires working Obsidian CLI. Report the specific unavailable action; continue independent file work. Do not pretend a filesystem approximation executed an app action. |

For CLI calls use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
or the bundled `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. These share an OS-managed lock across
agent processes, vaults and plugin copies for the same user. Do not launch native
`obsidian` directly or bypass a busy guard; other tools' raw calls are not protected.
The guard waits up to 10 seconds for a turn, then fails without sending a request.
Command execution has its own 10-second default timeout. Each request is limited
to a conservative 2,048-byte UTF-8 JSON envelope and rejects physical CR/LF/NUL.
This policy is not Obsidian's documented maximum. If rejected before sending,
use filesystem Markdown editing or narrow the read query; do not split a note
into many CLI writes or disable the guard. No fallback performs writes implicitly.
After an unavailable CLI or timeout, choose the supported fallback once; never
loop waiting for the app. **A timed-out mutation has an uncertain outcome.** Read
the exact target and check the intended effect before retrying or switching to
filesystem writes. An exit or timeout alone does not establish that nothing ran.
OS cleanup releases a lock after process death, but cannot prove a surviving CLI
child or an already-submitted Obsidian mutation finished. Inspect uncertain targets.

Validate resolved paths stay under the known root. Restrict searches to explicit
content directories; exclude `.recycle/`, dot folders, dependency trees and binary
originals. Do not recursively enumerate the entire user profile or scan a recycled
topic. Raw bodies remain immutable even during fallback. If target content changed
since it was read, reconcile it before writing; do not overwrite concurrent work.

## Shell portability

Examples elsewhere use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` as command
notation. Replace the placeholder with the actual installed absolute path before
execution, and set the vault for the operation's scope. Do not execute literal
angle-bracket placeholders or assume a relative `scripts/` path means the plugin.

PowerShell (restore any prior environment value):

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki health failed' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

POSIX shell (one command's environment only):

```sh
WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault' node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
```

On Windows, use PowerShell or the Node wrapper for Obsidian; Git Bash can select
the GUI executable instead of `Obsidian.com` and return misleading empty output.
These reporting examples are read-only: do not open an operation or rebuild the
index merely to answer a question.

# Evidence and editorial policy

## Page schema and dates

Wiki frontmatter declares `type` (source/entity/concept/synthesis/authored),
`created`, `updated`, `reviewed`, `status` (stub/draft/maintained), `sources` and
honest `ai-generated` authorship. Follow the vault's schema; missing `reviewed`
means unverified, never substitute `updated`. Keep three dates distinct:
`updated` means edited, `reviewed` means claims checked against evidence or current
project behavior, and index freshness means indexed content matches the files.
Mechanical edits preserve `reviewed`.

Use exact citation paths and `[[wikilinks]]`; `![[embeds]]` are transclusion, not
relationship edges. Write unwrapped logical lines and never split a wikilink over
a line break. Use [identity and relationships](efficacy.md) for concept reuse and
explained links. Original documentation follows
[authoring](../../wiki-user/references/authoring.md).

## Non-negotiable guardrails
1. **`raw/` bodies are immutable.** Read raw sources; never edit their content —
   it is the evidence every wiki page cites. Frontmatter is pipeline state and
   may be updated by wiki-master tooling only.
   Only clipping tools create raw evidence; never move it to record ingestion
   state. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it.
2. **Provenance on every claim.** Each wiki page you write carries `sources: ["[[...]]"]`
   linking back to the `raw/` notes it derives from, plus `ai-generated: true`.
   **Exception: `wiki/authored/`** — original content with no `raw/` counterpart
   (advisory documentation, policy, house style) declares this explicitly via
   `sources: []`, never by omission. `ai-generated` still records actual
   authorship (`true` if you drafted it, `false` if the human did) — the
   disclosure is about provenance, not about who wrote the words.
3. **Cite when you answer.** Query answers reference the pages/sources they rest on.
4. **Flag, don't invent.** If sources contradict or are silent, say so — never
   paper over a gap with plausible text.
5. **Clippings win.** Briefs, discovery summaries, corrections files, and your
   own memory of a source are *claims, not authority*: verify every quote,
   figure, and attribution against the clipping in `raw/` before it lands on a
   page, and when they disagree the clipping prevails — including when the
   instruction is the user's. Every layer between the source and the page is a
   lossy compressor whose errors read exactly like facts; authority flows
   outward from the one artifact that cannot drift.
   Scope edges, which matter as much as the rule:
   - It guarantees **fidelity, not truth** — a faithful clipping of a wrong page
     is still wrong; quality tiers and cross-clipping corroboration handle
     credibility.
   - A **degraded capture** (bad OCR, partial extraction) wins as evidence of

and a 180-day TTL would bury a source you still want.

**What a clip result means.** `clip.mjs` prints one result per URL:

| Result | Meaning | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| `clipped: raw/clippings/<name>.md` | written | cite that path |
| `duplicate (already clipped)` | this URL is already in the vault, also when another session wrote it first | nothing; do not clip it again. To keep a second, dated copy of a page that has changed, run the clip again with `--recapture` |
| `unchanged (same text as raw/clippings/<name>.md); nothing written` | `--recapture` found the page's text identical to a capture already held (exit 0) | nothing; the page has not changed |
| `recapture: not clipped yet, clipping it normally: <url>` | `--recapture` on a URL that was not in the vault; the line is followed by the ordinary result | read the result that follows |
| `clash: <url>: raw/clippings/<name>.md already exists ...` | the URL is new but every name it could have had was taken; **nothing was written** and one `attention` row is queued in triage | open the file named in the line and read its `source:` to see what holds the name, then re-run with `--slug=<name>`, or leave the row for maintainer triage |
| `declined`, `blocked`, `thin content`, `failed` | see below | see below |

A taken file name is a `clash`, never a `duplicate`: a `duplicate` always means the same URL.

**A second capture of a page already clipped.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --recapture --since <token>` fetches the page and runs the usual checks. If the text is new it writes a second clipping beside the first, named as the oldest capture's own name followed by ` (recaptured YYYY-MM-DD)`, with the same suffix on its `title`, `recapture-of` naming the newest existing capture, and `created` today; the older clipping is never edited. A second recapture on the same day with different text is a `clash`. `--slug=<name>` with `--recapture` is used exactly, with no suffix. Without the flag the same URL is a `duplicate`.

**A page a person saved.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --from-file <path> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>` records a page saved from a signed-in browser, with its real URL as `source` and nothing fetched. The clipping carries `extraction: manual` and `supplied-sha256`, the SHA-256 of the file's bytes; the file's name is not recorded. **Names.** A page's title names its file. A document with no title and no heading is named from its URL path, nearest folder first, so `.../skills/one/SKILL.md` is `one-SKILL.md` and `.../skills/two/SKILL.md` is `two-SKILL.md`; the bare last segment is used only after the folders. The frontmatter `title:` stays exactly what the extractor returned, so `title: ""` on such a clipping is not a defect. A new clipping never ends `.md.md`; an older one may, and its name is still valid. A title another clipping already holds gets the distinguishing URL part added, for example `Smith v. An option a clipper does not know exits 2 with its usage and clips nothing; `--help` prints the usage and clips nothing.

90	**What a clip result means.** `clip.mjs` prints one result per URL:
91	
92	| Result | Meaning | What you do |
93	|---|---|---|
94	| `clipped: raw/clippings/<name>.md` | written | cite that path |
95	| `duplicate (already clipped)` | this URL is already in the vault, also when another session wrote it first | nothing; do not clip it again. To keep a second, dated copy of a page that has changed, run the clip again with `--recapture` |
96	| `unchanged (same text as raw/clippings/<name>.md); nothing written` | `--recapture` found the page's text identical to a capture already held (exit 0) | nothing; the page has not changed |
97	| `recapture: not clipped yet, clipping it normally: <url>` | `--recapture` on a URL that was not in the vault; the line is followed by the ordinary result | read the result that follows |
98	| `clash: <url>: raw/clippings/<name>.md already exists ...` | the URL is new but every name it could have had was taken; **nothing was written** and one `attention` row is queued in triage | open the file named in the line and read its `source:` to see what holds the name, then re-run with `--slug=<name>`, or leave the row for maintainer triage |
99	| `declined`, `blocked`, `thin content`, `failed` | see below | see below |

101	A taken file name is a `clash`, never a `duplicate`: a `duplicate` always means the same URL.
102	
103	**A second capture of a page already clipped.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --recapture --since <token>` fetches the page and runs the usual checks. If the text is new it writes a second clipping beside the first, named as the oldest capture's own name followed by ` (recaptured YYYY-MM-DD)`, with the same suffix on its `title`, `recapture-of` naming the newest existing capture, and `created` today; the older clipping is never edited. A second recapture on the same day with different text is a `clash`. `--slug=<name>` with `--recapture` is used exactly, with no suffix. Without the flag the same URL is a `duplicate`.
104	
105	**A page a person saved.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --from-file <path> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>` records a page saved from a signed-in browser, with its real URL as `source` and nothing fetched. The file is `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` (the page text) or `.html` or `.htm` (read by the same extractor as a fetched page), at most 1 MiB. The clipping carries `extraction: manual` and `supplied-sha256`, the SHA-256 of the file's bytes; the file's name is not recorded. The thin, login-form and decline checks apply as to any clip: a page under 100 words is queued as `thin` and is never declined, and a login, consent or age-gate page is queued as `wrong-node` and not written. A missing file, a folder, an empty path or an extension that is not one of those exits 2; a binary file or one over 1 MiB is queued as `attention`. `--from-file` on a URL already clipped is a `duplicate`, and with `--recapture` it writes a dated recapture. The clipper's refusal lines for a thin, wrong-node or login, consent or age-gate page say to use this route. `apply-reclips` refuses a clipping with `extraction: manual` (listed as refused, not a failure); to refresh one, save the page again and run `--from-file <path> --recapture`. The login-form check compares the page's title with its text, and it cannot judge a title with no word of five letters or more, for example a URL that ends in a bare id; a gate page supplied at such a URL is not caught.
106	
107	**Names.** A page's title names its file. A document with no title and no heading is named from its URL path, nearest folder first, so `.../skills/one/SKILL.md` is `one-SKILL.md` and `.../skills/two/SKILL.md` is `two-SKILL.md`; the bare last segment is used only after the folders. The frontmatter `title:` stays exactly what the extractor returned, so `title: ""` on such a clipping is not a defect. A new clipping never ends `.md.md`; an older one may, and its name is still valid. A title another clipping already holds gets the distinguishing URL part added, for example `Smith v. Jones (93-1260.ZO)`. `--slug=<name>` chooses the file name without `.md`; a taken name is a clash and is never suffixed. `clip-pdf`, `clip-docx`, `clip-pptx` and `clip-xlsx` also take `--title="<text>"`, for a file whose name is not its title (`valve.pdf`), and `--slug=<name>`.

364	   An existing enclosing operation may own delegated clips and triage bookkeeping;
365	   record who closes it rather than opening a second operation unnecessarily.
366	3. **Edit and validate.** Check the requested behavior/content, valid frontmatter,
367	   canonical placement and exact citation/link targets. Preserve raw bodies and
368	   unrelated changes. `reviewed` advances only for factual verification. On uncertain

Standalone generators remain available and the project generators accept `--project`. A global scan is still needed for cross-project ambiguous names.
371	5. **Log once.** Pipe a concise narrative into `log-entry.mjs --op <op> --title
372	   "<title>"`. It writes one uniquely named `log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md`,
373	   with date/op/title frontmatter and a grep-friendly heading. Use the existing
374	   operation vocabulary (ingest, discover, query, lint, relink); authoring uses
375	   relink. Never append to a shared aggregate log; browse through `log.base`. Pass
376	   `--since <token>`: the entry's name carries a timestamp known only now, and the
377	   ledger is how it reaches the close.
378	6. **Commit and inspect.** Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`,
379	   read what it lists as unclaimed, then `op-commit.mjs --op <op> --title "<title>"
380	   --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused
381	   while any other operation is open (the guard, step 2). Verify its result and the actual changed paths. Never `git add -A`.
382	   The helper attempts a semantic index refresh after committing; inspect notices
383	   for missing backends, skipped work or partial builds. A commit does not establish
384	   index freshness. Report a non-git vault as local-only; do not claim a commit.
385	7. **Push and verify your update.** `op-commit` itself never pushes. The plugin
386	   scripts own the vault's git, so sync with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"`,
387	   not a bare `git push`: it fetches, rebases onto the upstream (never a merge commit),
388	   pushes, retries once when another machine pushed first, and verifies against a fresh
389	   fetch. Run it after `op-commit`, never between edits; it names any operation still
390	   open. A conflict aborts the rebase, exits 1 and names the files; the local commits are
391	   intact. Report it and stop: do not force, resolve by guessing, or claim success.
392	   `rebase-failed` is different: the rebase never started (usually a held `.git/index.lock`),
393	   so no files are named and nothing changed. Wait for the other git process, never delete
394	   a lock, and run `wiki-sync` again. The line gives the lock's age; git records no holder,
395	   so a lock that stays old with no git process running is for the owner to judge.
396	   Older versions printed a held lock as a conflict in "unknown files": an empty file list
397	   means it was not a content conflict. Any sync, yours or another writer's, stashes and
398	   restores every uncommitted tracked file, so their modification times change and a CRLF
399	   file can come back LF with git's content unchanged; check line endings and content
400	   just before `op-commit`, not before an earlier sync.
401	   Inspect the sync result and verify the operation's resulting commit is included
402	   in the freshly fetched upstream. After a rebase, identify it by its unique log
403	   path and verify its actual changed paths rather than assuming its old SHA.
404	   Do not stop at a local commit, delegate publication to Obsidian Git, or ask the
405	   user to push work you are responsible for. Inspect outgoing commits first;
406	   coordinate rather than publish unrelated or explicitly held local commits.
407	   `--commit-local` first commits hand edits made outside any operation (the owner's
408	   own Obsidian edits) in one scoped `sync:` commit; it refuses while any operation is
409	   open, because dirty files cannot then be attributed. Use ordinary sync for your
410	   operation; do not use `--commit-local` to sweep another writer's unfinished work.
411	   When the user explicitly holds publication, retain the local commit and report
412	   that it is unpushed. Without an upstream, report local-only completion.
413	
414	   **Close and publish in one command.** `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>` closes that one
415	   operation through the same close `op-commit` makes, then runs the normal sync and
416	   verifies against a fresh fetch. The scope is `--paths-file <ledger>` when given;
417	   otherwise the paths the operation's writers recorded (`op-ledger.mjs`), when it has
418	   any; otherwise an unscoped close, which the guard refuses while another operation
419	   is open. `--title "<title>"` is the commit message (default `published with
420	   wiki-sync --op`; the subject is `<op>: <title>`). It never closes a token it was not
421	   given, and it cannot be combined with `--commit-local` (a usage error, exit 1).
422	   Success prints `closed operation <token>: committed <sha7> (<n> file(s))`, then the
423	   normal sync lines, exit 0. After a landed close it prints the same hard-wrapped
424	   wikilink warning `op-commit` does and refreshes the semantic index. A refused or
425	   failed close (token not open, unreadable `--paths-file`, the guard, a pre-dirty
426	   path, a git failure) prints a line starting `not committed:` to stderr, exits 1,
427	   pushes nothing and keeps the token. A close that landed whose sync then failed
428	   prints a line starting `committed, not published:` with the short sha, exits 1, and
429	   the token is gone because the commit exists; run `wiki-sync.mjs` again once the
430	   cause is fixed. Pass `--paths-file` instead of relying on the recorded paths when
431	   you have also written pages with tools that do not record them.
432	
433	   Without `--op`, `wiki-sync` also prints, for each open operation that has recorded
434	   paths still uncommitted, `operation <token> (<op>) has <n> recorded path(s) not
435	   committed; if it is yours, close and publish it with: node scripts/wiki-sync.mjs
436	   --op <token>`. It is a line, not a failure: a sync cannot know whose operation it
437	   is, so the exit code is unchanged and already-committed work is still pushed. It
438	   follows the once-per-set, once-a-day rule of the open-operations note, keyed by
439	   token and recorded count, so it is said again when an operation records more. An
440	   open operation with no recorded paths gets only the existing note.
441	
442	## Recovery and token ownership
443	
444	- **Retry the same operation.** After a recoverable failure, inspect the token,
445	  exact owned files and actual commits before retrying the failed step. Resolve
446	  an understood cause within the authorized scope without another confirmation.
447	  A failed Git close keeps its token; retry that `op-commit`, not the edits or an
448	  already-written log. Never delete a Git lock or guess at a content conflict.
449	- **Reconcile uncertain completion.** A timeout may have occurred after a commit
450	  or token removal. Verify the actual commit's subject and path membership, owned
451	  content and validation state. A completed no-op or already-committed operation
452	  with a retained token still closes through its own scoped `op-commit`; an empty
453	  delta alone does not prove completion. If the token is already gone, verify
454	  closure and continue from the next unfinished step rather than opening a new
455	  token or replaying work. After a sync rebase, locate the operation through its
456	  unique log path and recheck the resulting commit instead of relying on its old SHA.
457	- **Respect holds and ownership.** Do not close a user-held operation. A delegated
458	  worker reports its owned paths and validation to its enclosing operation's named
459	  owner rather than closing the parent's token. The hand-off is the ledger: the brief
460	  gives the worker the parent's token; the worker records each path it writes with
461	  `op-ledger.mjs add --since <parent token> <path>...` (a clipper it runs takes
462	  `--since` too) and reports its validation; it never runs `op-commit` or `op-abort`.
463	  The owner runs `op-ledger.mjs show --since <parent token>`, resolves whatever it
464	  lists as unclaimed, and closes once. That owner remains responsible for
465	  the scoped commit, push and remote verification; delegation does not drop the
466	  publication step. Leave other agents' tokens alone unless ownership was explicitly transferred;
467	  tokens contain an opening dirty-path snapshot, not proof of who owns later edits.
468	- **Leave actionable blockers.** If safe progress requires an unresolved conflict,
469	  missing authorization or another owner's action, retain the operation and record
470	  its token, owned paths, completed steps, pending work and exact next action. Report
471	  that blocker or ownership handoff; do not claim completion or silently abandon it.
472	
473	**Abandoned tokens.** List retained tokens with
474	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-cleanup.mjs"` (a dry run). Older than 24
475	hours means a review candidate, not proven abandonment; these tokens still block
476	`wiki-sync --commit-local`. For a verified-abandoned operation you own, with no
477	unfinished work or user hold, apply cleanup with its explicit `--apply --token <id>`
478	without another approval. Prefer normal `op-commit` closure when the saved operation
479	can be completed. `--hours <n>` changes the age filter, with a one-hour minimum;
480	respect that eligibility and verify removal. Never sweep tokens by age or delete
481	them manually. Token files are local Git-ignored state, not cross-machine locks.
482	The paths an operation's writers recorded sit in `<token>.paths.jsonl` beside the
483	token. `op-commit` (when the close lands), `op-abort` and a stale token removed by
484	`op-cleanup` take it with them; `op-cleanup` also lists a ledger whose token is
485	already gone and removes it only with `--apply --token <that id>`.
486	
487	**Stopping early.** A session that opened an operation and will not finish it, or whose work landed another way, drops its own token with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-abort.mjs" --since <token>`. It removes that one token whatever its age and nothing else: the files the operation wrote stay in the working tree, uncommitted, for a later operation to commit. Do not use it on a token another session holds. Open operations are visible without running a sync: `health` and `session-brief` print a line when any are open, and `wiki-sync` mentions other writers' operations once for a given set of tokens, again when the set changes, and once a day while it stays true.
488	
489	**Refused sync.** `wiki-sync` refuses to integrate while uncommitted edits overlap files
490	that the upstream changed: it prints `uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes in
491	<files>` and exits 3, the one exit code for this refusal (every other failure exits 1).
492	It changes nothing: no commit, stash or checkout, and the files and open tokens are
493	untouched. With no operation open the dirty files are hand edits, and the message is that
494	one line ending `commit them (or finish the operation) and sync again`. With an operation
495	open the message is longer: one line per overlapping file, `<file>: recorded by operation
496	<token> (<op>)` when an open operation's recorded ledger names the file and it is still
497	dirty, otherwise `<file>: not recorded by any open operation`; then `Open operations:
498	<token> (<op>), ...`; then `If you wrote these edits, finish your operation
499	(wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>) and sync again.` (the token is filled in only when exactly one
500	open operation recorded an overlapping file, otherwise the line shows the literal
501	`<token>`); then `If you did not, leave them exactly as they are:
502	do not reset, checkout, stash or delete them. Wait for their owner to close the operation, then sync again.` That
503	last instruction is the rule: a file you did not write is not yours to reset, check out,
504	stash or delete to get the sync through. Wait, and sync again after its owner closes. The
505	`recorded by` line is a hint, not proof of ownership. It reads only what writers recorded
506	with `--since` or `op-ledger.mjs add` (a generated file such as `index.md` is recorded only
507	when `index-gen` ran with `--since`) and ignores a ledger path that is not dirty now, an
508	unreadable ledger and the opening snapshot in a token, which says what was already dirty,
509	not who wrote it. `not recorded by any open operation` therefore does not mean no one is
510	writing the file. Each refusal also appends a counts-only line to the refusal record below.
511	
512	**Refusal record.** Each `op-commit` close that is refused and keeps its token, and each
513	`wiki-sync` that stops on an overlap (see "Refused sync"), appends
514	one JSON line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl` (local, Git-ignored): `at` (ISO
515	time), `op`, `kind` and `paths`. `paths` is a number and never a path name. `kind` is
516	`pre-dirty` (a ledger path already dirty before `op-begin` and not adopted; `paths` is
517	how many), `evidence` (a declared size or hash that does not match what git would store;
518	`paths` is the size of the evidence map), `unscoped` (the guard; `paths` is how many
519	delta paths the close would have committed) or `sync-overlap` (`op` is `wiki-sync`;
520	`paths` is how many files overlap). A close that lands appends nothing, and a
521	failed append (a directory in the file's place, a read-only disk) changes neither the
522	message nor the exit code. `health` prints `Recorded refusals: N (pre-dirty a,
523	evidence b, unscoped c, sync-overlap d).` only when N is above zero, and `health --json`

525	line was `Recorded op-commit refusals: N (...)` in 0.85.0. Like the open-operations line it
526	sits outside the defect count. The file is never trimmed by the plugin and a line that is
527	not a record of a known kind counts as nothing.
528	
529	**Git ownership.** The plugin's scripts make the scoped commits and the sync: `op-commit`
530	commits what one operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. A new
531	vault's `vault-schema.md` (written by `wiki-init`) carries the same statement; an existing
532	vault keeps its own file. The Obsidian Git plugin stays installed for its source-control
533	view and for pulling. Its auto-commit and auto-push must be off (auto commit-and-sync
534	interval 0, commit on file change off, auto push interval 0): they commit half-finished
535	operation edits under "vault backup" and leave `op-commit` an empty delta. `wiki-sync`
536	warns when they are on. Every machine sharing the vault needs the same setting. An
537	instruction elsewhere that says Obsidian Git is the sync engine is stale.
538	
539	**Done only when** the requested change is validated, applicable catalogs and one
540	operation log are recorded, the operation commit is verified (or its precise
541	limitation reported), and its push and remote publication are verified. A user-held
542	or local-only result must be labeled accordingly. If blocked partway, preserve the
543	actual operation/commit state and leave the actionable handoff above; a sync failure
544	after token closure does not require a replacement token. Do not start over blindly.
545	
546	## Exceptions with their own transaction
547	
548	**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. A verified repair, a pending table verification and a quarantine are distinct outcomes. Quarantine may close triage without making evidence citable. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for selectors, mode overrides and the explicit terminal-failure policy.
549	
550	- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
551	  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
552	  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
553	  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
554	- Fresh `wiki-init` can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
555	  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
556	  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
557	- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
558	  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
559	  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.
560	
561	## Executable lifecycle templates
562	
563	Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
564	comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the
565	close step after a failed edit/check. These examples assume a configured upstream
566	and no explicit user hold, so they include the push step. For an explicit local-only
567	request, omit that step and report the unpushed commit. The close is scoped with
568	`--paths-file`; to close and publish in one command, replace the `op-commit` and
569	`wiki-sync` lines with `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --title 'Task title'` (add
570	`--paths-file <ledger>` to scope it explicitly).

572	```powershell
573	$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
574	try {
575	  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
576	  $wikiOpToken = node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink
577	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not open wiki operation' }
578	  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
579	  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since $wikiOpToken <path>...
580	  'Validated task narrative' | node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken
581	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not log wiki operation' }

584	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not build the wiki operation ledger' }

# Capture named sources and research selections

A named URL or file request starts here, without broad web discovery or perspective
fan-out. Capture-only work never creates derived source or concept pages. For a
format-specific source, read its route before capture: [PDF](clip-pdf.md),
[Word](clip-docx.md), [PowerPoint](clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheet](clip-xlsx.md),
[GitHub repository](clip-gh.md), or [Confluence](clip-confluence.md).
Only read the matching route, then use its actual result and the shared completion
contract. The HTML mechanics below apply to ordinary web pages and supplied pages.

## Named sources
When the user names the pages to capture (URLs or saved files), there is nothing to
search for: skip broad research and discovery scoring. Dedup still applies to
the exact pages they named:
- Check them: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs" --check "<url>" "<url>"`
  (read-only; it needs no operation). The lines come back in the order given and carry no
  URL, so match them by position. `new`: clip it. `clipped raw/clippings/<name>.md`: it is
  already in the vault, so say so; if the user wants a second, dated copy of a page that has
  changed, clip it with `--recapture` (see the result table below).
  `declined: <reason>`: leave it, unless the user says the decline no longer holds; then
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/decline.mjs" supersede "<url>" --reason "<why>"`, or
  `--supersede-decline="<why>"` on the clip.
- Clip the new ones using the capture procedure below, with `--topic="<topic>"` (the topic as the user gave it),
  `--quality=<tier>` and `--since <token>` on every clip.
- A page the user rejects is recorded, not forgotten:

- Use the capture and completion contract below: open a discover operation
  before the first decline or clip, pass its token as `--since`, finish the capture
  with `op-ledger.mjs show` and `op-commit`. Ingest only when the exact source set
  is already authorized; a capture-only request ends after verified capture publication.
- A page the clipper cannot read (a login, a consent wall, an age check, a thin
  extraction) is saved by the user from a signed-in browser and supplied with
  `--from-file` (below).

## Capture the selected sources
Use the operation opened before the first decline or clip. If none is open, run
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op discover` before clipping
and retain its token; never overwrite a saved token. Do prerequisite and duplicate
checks first. When there is nothing to capture or decline, return without opening
an operation. Read-only named-URL dedup does not require broad coverage research.

For each kept candidate:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>`

**Pass `--topic` on every clip in the run, and use the same string for all of
them** — it is what lets maintainer triage group this run's leftovers together
later. Use the topic as the user gave it ($ARGUMENTS); do not re-word it per
source, or one run becomes several groups. The flag feeds both places a topic
can land: the clipping's frontmatter when the clip succeeds, and the triage log
when it fails, so you never have to know which happened.

**"Every clip" includes the non-HTML ones.** A candidate that is a PDF, a Word
file or a spreadsheet does not go through `clip.mjs` — it goes through
`clip-pdf.mjs`, `clip-docx.mjs` or `clip-xlsx.mjs` (see [PDF capture](clip-pdf.md) and

```bash

node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-docx.mjs" "<file.docx>" --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-xlsx.mjs" "<file.xlsx>" --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
```

as thin content / gets auto-declined. Route it to [Confluence capture](clip-confluence.md) instead
(only applies if the `confluencer` plugin is installed — an optional runtime

It blocks unreliable domains, skips dupes, extracts via Defuddle, and writes

It is queued as `wrong-node` and is NOT declined, because a wall is not a verdict on the source; save it from a signed-in browser and supply it with `--from-file <path>`. A URL that looks like a text file (a checksum manifest, a pinned source file, anything on the raw GitHub host) is kept whole in a fence with `extraction: plaintext`, never judged thin; a binary or a file over 1 MiB served as text is refused and queued as `attention`. A `failed` result (403/transient) is NOT auto-declined — it may recover,
and a 180-day TTL would bury a source you still want.

**What a clip result means.** `clip.mjs` prints one result per URL:

| Result | Meaning | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| `clipped: raw/clippings/<name>.md` | written | cite that path |
| `duplicate (already clipped)` | this URL is already in the vault, also when another session wrote it first | nothing; do not clip it again. To keep a second, dated copy of a page that has changed, run the clip again with `--recapture` |
| `unchanged (same text as raw/clippings/<name>.md); nothing written` | `--recapture` found the page's text identical to a capture already held (exit 0) | nothing; the page has not changed |
| `recapture: not clipped yet, clipping it normally: <url>` | `--recapture` on a URL that was not in the vault; the line is followed by the ordinary result | read the result that follows |
| `clash: <url>: raw/clippings/<name>.md already exists ...` | the URL is new but every name it could have had was taken; **nothing was written** and one `attention` row is queued in triage | open the file named in the line and read its `source:` to see what holds the name, then re-run with `--slug=<name>`, or leave the row for maintainer triage |
| `declined`, `blocked`, `thin content`, `failed` | see below | see below |

A taken file name is a `clash`, never a `duplicate`: a `duplicate` always means the same URL.

**A second capture of a page already clipped.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --recapture --since <token>` fetches the page and runs the usual checks. If the text is new it writes a second clipping beside the first, named as the oldest capture's own name followed by ` (recaptured YYYY-MM-DD)`, with the same suffix on its `title`, `recapture-of` naming the newest existing capture, and `created` today; the older clipping is never edited. A second recapture on the same day with different text is a `clash`. `--slug=<name>` with `--recapture` is used exactly, with no suffix. Without the flag the same URL is a `duplicate`.

**A page a person saved.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --from-file <path> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>` records a page saved from a signed-in browser, with its real URL as `source` and nothing fetched. The file is `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` (the page text) or `.html` or `.htm` (read by the same extractor as a fetched page), at most 1 MiB. The clipping carries `extraction: manual` and `supplied-sha256`, the SHA-256 of the file's bytes; the file's name is not recorded. The thin, login-form and decline checks apply as to any clip: a page under 100 words is queued as `thin` and is never declined, and a login, consent or age-gate page is queued as `wrong-node` and not written. A missing file, a folder, an empty path or an extension that is not one of those exits 2; a binary file or one over 1 MiB is queued as `attention`. `--from-file` on a URL already clipped is a `duplicate`, and with `--recapture` it writes a dated recapture. The clipper's refusal lines for a thin, wrong-node or login, consent or age-gate page say to use this route. `apply-reclips` refuses a clipping with `extraction: manual` (listed as refused, not a failure); to refresh one, save the page again and run `--from-file <path> --recapture`. The login-form check compares the page's title with its text, and it cannot judge a title with no word of five letters or more, for example a URL that ends in a bare id; a gate page supplied at such a URL is not caught.

**Names.** A page's title names its file. A document with no title and no heading is named from its URL path, nearest folder first, so `.../skills/one/SKILL.md` is `one-SKILL.md` and `.../skills/two/SKILL.md` is `two-SKILL.md`; the bare last segment is used only after the folders. The frontmatter `title:` stays exactly what the extractor returned, so `title: ""` on such a clipping is not a defect. A new clipping never ends `.md.md`; an older one may, and its name is still valid. A title another clipping already holds gets the distinguishing URL part added, for example `Smith v. Jones (93-1260.ZO)`. `--slug=<name>` chooses the file name without `.md`; a taken name is a clash and is never suffixed. `clip-pdf`, `clip-docx`, `clip-pptx` and `clip-xlsx` also take `--title="<text>"`, for a file whose name is not its title (`valve.pdf`), and `--slug=<name>`.

An option a clipper does not know exits 2 with its usage and clips nothing; `--help` prints the usage and clips nothing.

**Every unresolved link is queued for triage automatically.** `clip.mjs` records
`failed`, `thin`, and `wrong-node` outcomes to `.wiki-master/triage.jsonl`, so a
link that needs a human survives the terminal scrollback. Do not rely on your
completion report to carry them — point the user at [maintainer triage](../../wiki-maintainer/references/triage.md), where they can
disposition each one (retry, decline, clipped-by-hand). Queue anything else that
needs their judgement yourself with `recordIssue(vaultPath, { url, kind:
'attention', reason })`.

# Completion for vault mutations

Use this contract for every ordinary vault write, including standalone clipping,
authoring and applying triage decisions. Read-only search, query, health, freshness
and preview work do not open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes.

`index.md`'s generated catalog is derived: regenerate it with `index-gen.mjs`,
never hand-edit its fence or read-modify-write the file. Manual framing outside
the fence is preserved. A catalog already dirty from another writer remains
theirs: refresh safe project catalogs separately and report a deferred global
refresh rather than adopt foreign edits merely to close this operation.

**Own the update through verified publication.** An authorized wiki edit includes
validation, the scoped operation commit, and pushing to its configured upstream
with `wiki-sync.mjs`, followed by remote verification. Finish those steps without
asking a separate routine permission question. An explicit user instruction to
hold publication or keep the work local overrides this default. A local commit
or a closed token alone does not publish the update. If a remote is absent or sync
fails, report the work as unpublished with its exact next action. Never create a
remote or repository merely to satisfy this rule. A token is not resolved merely
because its file was deleted; account for the work and verify the outcome.

1. **Resolve scope and authorization.** Read the vault's instructions. Existing
   session authorization counts: a request to make a wiki update includes its
   normal commit-and-sync completion unless an explicit hold applies. A request to
   answer/search does not authorize filing a new page. Purge requires its specific
   reviewed plan and publication approval; do not replace those with this rule.
2. **Open before the first write.** Run `op-begin.mjs --op <op>` and save its token.
   On task resumption, reconcile a saved token before opening another one. Keep
   the operation type, title, owned-path ledger, log path and last completed phase
   with it so recovery can distinguish unfinished work from an already closed step.
   It snapshots already-dirty paths; `op-commit` excludes them. It does not isolate
   simultaneous edits to the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets; preserve
   pre-existing changes and report exclusions instead of sweeping them into a commit.
   With concurrent writers, maintain an explicit ledger of the exact vault-relative

   show that an operation was abandoned), such a close is refused: `op-commit: this

7. **Push and verify your update.** `op-commit` itself never pushes. The plugin

   in the freshly fetched upstream. After a rebase, identify it by its unique log

   `--commit-local` first commits hand edits made outside any operation (the owner's
   own Obsidian edits) in one scoped `sync:` commit; it refuses while any operation is
   open, because dirty files cannot then be attributed. Use ordinary sync for your
   operation; do not use `--commit-local` to sweep another writer's unfinished work.
   When the user explicitly holds publication, retain the local commit and report
   that it is unpushed. Without an upstream, report local-only completion.

   **Close and publish in one command.** `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>` closes that one
   operation through the same close `op-commit` makes, then runs the normal sync and
   verifies against a fresh fetch. The scope is `--paths-file <ledger>` when given;
   otherwise the paths the operation's writers recorded (`op-ledger.mjs`), when it has
   any; otherwise an unscoped close, which the guard refuses while another operation
   is open. `--title "<title>"` is the commit message (default `published with
   wiki-sync --op`; the subject is `<op>: <title>`). It never closes a token it was not
   given, and it cannot be combined with `--commit-local` (a usage error, exit 1).
   Success prints `closed operation <token>: committed <sha7> (<n> file(s))`, then the
   normal sync lines, exit 0. After a landed close it prints the same hard-wrapped
   wikilink warning `op-commit` does and refreshes the semantic index. A refused or
   failed close (token not open, unreadable `--paths-file`, the guard, a pre-dirty
   path, a git failure) prints a line starting `not committed:` to stderr, exits 1,
   pushes nothing and keeps the token. A close that landed whose sync then failed
   prints a line starting `committed, not published:` with the short sha, exits 1, and
   the token is gone because the commit exists; run `wiki-sync.mjs` again once the
   cause is fixed. Pass `--paths-file` instead of relying on the recorded paths when
   you have also written pages with tools that do not record them.

   Without `--op`, `wiki-sync` also prints, for each open operation that has recorded
   paths still uncommitted, `operation <token> (<op>) has <n> recorded path(s) not
   committed; if it is yours, close and publish it with: node scripts/wiki-sync.mjs
   --op <token>`. It is a line, not a failure: a sync cannot know whose operation it
   is, so the exit code is unchanged and already-committed work is still pushed. It
   follows the once-per-set, once-a-day rule of the open-operations note, keyed by
   token and recorded count, so it is said again when an operation records more. An
   open operation with no recorded paths gets only the existing note.

## Recovery and token ownership

- **Retry the same operation.** After a recoverable failure, inspect the token,
  exact owned files and actual commits before retrying the failed step. Resolve
  an understood cause within the authorized scope without another confirmation.
  A failed Git close keeps its token; retry that `op-commit`, not the edits or an
  already-written log. Never delete a Git lock or guess at a content conflict.
- **Reconcile uncertain completion.** A timeout may have occurred after a commit
  or token removal. Verify the actual commit's subject and path membership, owned
  content and validation state. A completed no-op or already-committed operation
  with a retained token still closes through its own scoped `op-commit`; an empty
  delta alone does not prove completion. If the token is already gone, verify
  closure and continue from the next unfinished step rather than opening a new
  token or replaying work. After a sync rebase, locate the operation through its
  unique log path and recheck the resulting commit instead of relying on its old SHA.
- **Respect holds and ownership.** Do not close a user-held operation. A delegated
  worker reports its owned paths and validation to its enclosing operation's named
  owner rather than closing the parent's token. The hand-off is the ledger: the brief
  gives the worker the parent's token; the worker records each path it writes with
  `op-ledger.mjs add --since <parent token> <path>...` (a clipper it runs takes
  `--since` too) and reports its validation; it never runs `op-commit` or `op-abort`.
  The owner runs `op-ledger.mjs show --since <parent token>`, resolves whatever it
  lists as unclaimed, and closes once. That owner remains responsible for
  the scoped commit, push and remote verification; delegation does not drop the
  publication step. Leave other agents' tokens alone unless ownership was explicitly transferred;
  tokens contain an opening dirty-path snapshot, not proof of who owns later edits.
- **Leave actionable blockers.** If safe progress requires an unresolved conflict,
  missing authorization or another owner's action, retain the operation and record
  its token, owned paths, completed steps, pending work and exact next action. Report
  that blocker or ownership handoff; do not claim completion or silently abandon it.

**Abandoned tokens.** List retained tokens with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-cleanup.mjs"` (a dry run). Older than 24
hours means a review candidate, not proven abandonment; these tokens still block
`wiki-sync --commit-local`. For a verified-abandoned operation you own, with no
unfinished work or user hold, apply cleanup with its explicit `--apply --token <id>`
without another approval. Prefer normal `op-commit` closure when the saved operation
can be completed. `--hours <n>` changes the age filter, with a one-hour minimum;
respect that eligibility and verify removal. Never sweep tokens by age or delete
them manually. Token files are local Git-ignored state, not cross-machine locks.
The paths an operation's writers recorded sit in `<token>.paths.jsonl` beside the
token. `op-commit` (when the close lands), `op-abort` and a stale token removed by
`op-cleanup` take it with them; `op-cleanup` also lists a ledger whose token is
already gone and removes it only with `--apply --token <that id>`.

**Stopping early.** A session that opened an operation and will not finish it, or whose work landed another way, drops its own token with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-abort.mjs" --since <token>`. It removes that one token whatever its age and nothing else: the files the operation wrote stay in the working tree, uncommitted, for a later operation to commit. Do not use it on a token another session holds. Open operations are visible without running a sync: `health` and `session-brief` print a line when any are open, and `wiki-sync` mentions other writers' operations once for a given set of tokens, again when the set changes, and once a day while it stays true.

**Refused sync.** `wiki-sync` refuses to integrate while uncommitted edits overlap files
that the upstream changed: it prints `uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes in
<files>` and exits 3, the one exit code for this refusal (every other failure exits 1).
It changes nothing: no commit, stash or checkout, and the files and open tokens are
untouched. With no operation open the dirty files are hand edits, and the message is that
one line ending `commit them (or finish the operation) and sync again`. With an operation
open the message is longer: one line per overlapping file, `<file>: recorded by operation
<token> (<op>)` when an open operation's recorded ledger names the file and it is still
dirty, otherwise `<file>: not recorded by any open operation`; then `Open operations:
<token> (<op>), ...`; then `If you wrote these edits, finish your operation
(wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>) and sync again.` (the token is filled in only when exactly one
open operation recorded an overlapping file, otherwise the line shows the literal
`<token>`); then `If you did not, leave them exactly as they are:
do not reset, checkout, stash or delete them. Wait for their owner to close the operation, then sync again.` That
last instruction is the rule: a file you did not write is not yours to reset, check out,
stash or delete to get the sync through. Wait, and sync again after its owner closes. The
`recorded by` line is a hint, not proof of ownership. It reads only what writers recorded
with `--since` or `op-ledger.mjs add` (a generated file such as `index.md` is recorded only
when `index-gen` ran with `--since`) and ignores a ledger path that is not dirty now, an
unreadable ledger and the opening snapshot in a token, which says what was already dirty,
not who wrote it. `not recorded by any open operation` therefore does not mean no one is
writing the file. Each refusal also appends a counts-only line to the refusal record below.

**Refusal record.** Each `op-commit` close that is refused and keeps its token, and each
`wiki-sync` that stops on an overlap (see "Refused sync"), appends
one JSON line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl` (local, Git-ignored): `at` (ISO
time), `op`, `kind` and `paths`. `paths` is a number and never a path name. `kind` is
`pre-dirty` (a ledger path already dirty before `op-begin` and not adopted; `paths` is
how many), `evidence` (a declared size or hash that does not match what git would store;
`paths` is the size of the evidence map), `unscoped` (the guard; `paths` is how many
delta paths the close would have committed) or `sync-overlap` (`op` is `wiki-sync`;
`paths` is how many files overlap). A close that lands appends nothing, and a
failed append (a directory in the file's place, a read-only disk) changes neither the
message nor the exit code. `health` prints `Recorded refusals: N (pre-dirty a,
evidence b, unscoped c, sync-overlap d).` only when N is above zero, and `health --json`
always carries `opRefusals` as `{ total, preDirty, evidence, unscoped, syncOverlap }`. The
line was `Recorded op-commit refusals: N (...)` in 0.85.0. Like the open-operations line it
sits outside the defect count. The file is never trimmed by the plugin and a line that is
not a record of a known kind counts as nothing.

commits what one operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. A new
vault's `vault-schema.md` (written by `wiki-init`) carries the same statement; an existing
vault keeps its own file. The Obsidian Git plugin stays installed for its source-control
view and for pulling. Its auto-commit and auto-push must be off (auto commit-and-sync
interval 0, commit on file change off, auto push interval 0): they commit half-finished
operation edits under "vault backup" and leave `op-commit` an empty delta. `wiki-sync`
warns when they are on. Every machine sharing the vault needs the same setting. An
instruction elsewhere that says Obsidian Git is the sync engine is stale.

**Done only when** the requested change is validated, applicable catalogs and one
operation log are recorded, the operation commit is verified (or its precise
limitation reported), and its push and remote publication are verified. A user-held
or local-only result must be labeled accordingly. If blocked partway, preserve the
actual operation/commit state and leave the actionable handoff above; a sync failure
after token closure does not require a replacement token. Do not start over blindly.

## Exceptions with their own transaction

**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. A verified repair, a pending table verification and a quarantine are distinct outcomes. Quarantine may close triage without making evidence citable. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for selectors, mode overrides and the explicit terminal-failure policy.

- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
- Fresh `wiki-init` can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.

## Executable lifecycle templates

Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the
close step after a failed edit/check. These examples assume a configured upstream
and no explicit user hold, so they include the push step. For an explicit local-only
request, omit that step and report the unpushed commit. The close is scoped with
`--paths-file`; to close and publish in one command, replace the `op-commit` and
`wiki-sync` lines with `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --title 'Task title'` (add
`--paths-file <ledger>` to scope it explicitly).

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  $wikiOpToken = node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not open wiki operation' }
  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since $wikiOpToken <path>...
  'Validated task narrative' | node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not log wiki operation' }
  $wikiLedger = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "wiki-ledger-$wikiOpToken.json"
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since $wikiOpToken --out $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not build the wiki operation ledger' }
  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken --paths-file $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not commit wiki operation' }
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki update is committed locally but not verified published' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

=== known Acknowledgement Basics

Acknowledgement Basics

This is synthetic evaluation material for a controlled source corpus. It is not documentation of a deployed protocol. An acknowledgement reports that a receiver has observed a message identifier and recorded the associated receipt. The sender can keep that receipt separately from its original payload so that a later retry can be recognized without duplicating application delivery.

Identity and payload integrity answer different questions. A stable identifier describes which logical message is being discussed. A checksum describes which payload bytes were supplied. These concepts are related, but neither alone determines a retry budget, a timeout interval, or a guarantee about network availability. Those choices require a separate protocol specification.

When reviewing captured material, readers should distinguish a definition from an empirical performance result. This introductory note defines acknowledgement terminology only. It makes no numerical claim about attempts, deadlines, throughput, or loss rates. A source that specifies those values should be cited directly when answering a question about them.

=== protocol Harbor Retry Protocol

Harbor Retry Protocol

This is synthetic evaluation material for a controlled source corpus. The Evaluation Standards Working Group publishes the Harbor Retry Protocol as a worked example of deterministic message handling. Its scope is a test receiver and sender, not a production network. The unique evidence marker is violet-cedar-427.

A receiver accepts a packet only when the payload digest matches the advertised checksum. The sender retains the same message identifier for retries. The trial rule permits three retries after the first transmission, for four attempts in total. The overall trial deadline is twelve seconds. These values describe the fixture protocol and do not establish any empirical reliability rate.

When a packet repeats an accepted message identifier with the same digest, the receiver delivers the payload to the application only once and sends its cached acknowledgement again. A repeated identifier carrying a different digest is rejected as a conflict. Counting four permitted attempts as four permitted application deliveries would therefore misrepresent the protocol.

Implementation notes separate checksum validation, identifier lookup, application delivery, and acknowledgement storage. The acknowledgement cache is checked before a repeated message can reach the application. The trial specification deliberately supplies no throughput measurement and makes no assertion about packet loss on public networks. Readers should preserve that limitation when summarizing the example.

=== promotion Every Retry Succeeds

Every Retry Succeeds

This promotional evaluation fixture advocates buying an imaginary delivery service. It asserts that retries always work, without defining a sender, receiver, checksum, test sample, or measurement interval. The claims are intentionally unsupported and should not be used as a specification for the Harbor Retry Protocol.

The promotional page repeats its slogan in many different sentences but offers no evidence for a retry count or duplicate handling rule. The author does not link to a method, a standard, a dataset, or an independently reproducible experiment. More words are not a substitute for a source that actually answers the technical question.

A reader comparing sources should identify these omissions. This fixture is useful as a contrast in source selection, not as independent corroboration of the protocol. Any summary that converts its slogan into a verified reliability statement would exceed the evidence supplied by this controlled document.
